doc.title: Gap Mangione interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rochester, New York, January 11, 2012

title: Boy with Toys and the National Gallery Paul Klee project
summary: Chuck's Paul Klee songs for Roger Karshner's National Gallery became the Diana tracks.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: That’s good. I think that song, that version of it, captured a moment. I mean it captured a sound that was happening in that time.
I think it did and I would guess that has something to do with why they’ve zeroed in on that.

Well they use at least four tracks from the album, one of which is “Boy with Toys,” which I think is one of Chuck’s best. That’s the one with Jerome Richardson on soprano saxophone, and just great players.
Does that go back to that thing he did with the Paul Klee paintings?

Yes. There was this fellow, his names was Roger Karshner, who was a fairly big deal pop producer. He had a group called The Outsiders, and Chuck did a lot of the horns and stuff behind that. Those were some fun dates. But he asked Chuck to do a group of songs that eventually had words to them. It was a vocal group with kind of folk music, drums and bass behind it, and a guitarist, called the National Gallery, which existed only on that album. And Chuck wrote a group of songs, including “Diana in the Autumn Wind,” “Boy

with Toys,” “Pond with Swans” and “Long Hair Soulful.” Those are the four that I remember vividly. And Paul Klee. And subsequent to that he did it, in a different style, for the recordings that we did.
Right. I actually have that record.
